headline: Figma Goes Agentic This Month
subheadline: Figma's May release introduces agents, MCP workflows, and write-to-canvas — directly relevant to the MCP + Claude integration you're building. Plus: Claude Design wants to eat Figma's lunch.

sections.label: Watch
sections.title: Figma May 2026 Release Notes: Agents, MCP, and Write to Canvas
sections.description: This is the big one. Figma's May release livestream walks through agents, MCP, skills, and write-to-canvas workflows. Given you're actively building a Figma MCP + Claude integration for white-label sport apps, this isn't optional viewing — it'll directly shape what's possible in your architecture. Pay attention to how they frame 'skills' as composable agent capabilities.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Figma May 2026 Release Notes — Full Written Breakdown
sections.description: The official docs companion to the video above. Covers agents, MCP, skills, and write-to-canvas with actual workflow examples. Bookmark this — you'll want to reference it when wiring up your Claude integration. The three walkthrough workflows start from design system foundations, which is exactly your world.

sections.label: Trending
sections.title: Claude Design: Anthropic's Play to Replace Figma
sections.description: Anthropic launched Claude Design on April 17 — turn prompts into prototypes, decks, and mockups directly in Claude. This is worth watching not as a Figma replacement (you're way too deep for that), but as a signal of where AI-native design is headed. Also relevant because it tells you what Anthropic thinks designers want from Claude — useful context for your MCP integration work.

sections.label: Listen
sections.title: The Future of MCP — David Soria Parra, Anthropic
sections.description: Anthropic's David Soria Parra lays out where MCP is headed in 2026 and how it fits into the broader agent ecosystem. Perfect stroller listen. Since you're building on Figma MCP + Claude, hearing Anthropic's own roadmap vision for MCP will help you make better architecture decisions now instead of refactoring later.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Automating Design Systems with AI: Tokens, Governance, and Agents
sections.description: A practical guide to using AI agents for design system governance — automated token management, consistency checks, component generation. Directly maps to your design system work. The section on Figma tokens + AI agents is particularly relevant for the white-label sport apps system where you need consistency across multiple brand configurations.

sections.label: Try this tool
sections.title: Figma Make: Voice-to-Text Prompts & Zapier Connector
sections.description: Figma Make just shipped voice-to-text prompts, question cards for better context gathering, version history, and a Zapier connector. The Zapier bit is interesting — it could let you pipe external data (like sport event feeds or CRM data) into Make without building custom integrations. Worth a quick explore this week.

sections.label: Concept of the day
sections.title: AI-Orchestrated Design Systems
sections.description: The shift from 'design system as component library' to 'design system as AI-orchestrated ecosystem' is real. Instead of humans manually enforcing token usage, naming conventions, and component consistency, AI agents now handle governance — flagging drift, suggesting corrections, even auto-generating variants. The interesting debate: some teams report needing engineering code review for AI-generated components, which partly defeats the purpose. As someone building this exact infrastructure, you're in a position to get the balance right.

sections.label: Think about this
sections.title: When you return, will your title matter less than your stack?
sections.description: You left as Group Head of Design. You're coming back as someone who can build with Cursor, ship with Lovable, wire agents through MCP, and architect AI-augmented design systems. The industry is splitting between designers who direct AI and designers who still hand off static screens. Which role do you actually want to return to — and does a traditional design leadership title even capture what you do now?
